summary: Master WASH programme design, logframes, JMP indicators, and M&E systems. 5-day hands-on training with KoBoToolbox and Power BI. Enrol at TrainingCred.
lede: Planning and assessing water, sanitation and hygiene programmes helps mid-career practitioners turn identified needs into measurable interventions. Participants learn to develop theories of change and logframes, select equity-sensitive indicators, design needs assessments and digital data collection, and evaluate results against OECD-DAC criteria. The course also covers monitoring systems and reporting results to donors, government counterparts, and communities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career professionals working across the WASH sector in development, humanitarian, and government contexts who are responsible for designing, implementing, or evaluating water, sanitation, and hygiene programmes.
modules: WASH Sector Context and Programme Foundations
Theory of Change and Logframe Construction
WASH Indicator Development and Results Frameworks
Digital Data Collection for WASH Monitoring
WASH Programme Evaluation Design and Methods
Data Analysis, Reporting, and Donor Communication
prerequisites: To get the most from this course, participants should meet the following requirements: Experience: Minimum one year of practical experience in a WASH programme, M&E, or project management role in a development or humanitarian context; Prior knowledge: Working familiarity with logframe concepts and basic field data collection methods; no advanced statistics or coding required; Equipment: A laptop with a modern web browser and internet access is required for KoBoToolbox and Power BI lab sessions; Pre-course setup: Create a free KoBoToolbox account at kobotoolbox.org before Day 1; course facilitators will send setup instructions in advance; Language: Course is delivered in English; participants should be comfortable reading and writing technical documents in English
